children: to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase in more than three years.
"An attitude of optimism is exactly what I heard at this week's meeting," he said.
As he said at the Jackson Hole speech last month, Warsh would be “hard-pressed” to describe financial conditions as restrictive.
Core PCE for September is estimated to be about 3.2%. Too many categories are still trending higher than the Fed's 2% inflation goal, he added.
"We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving toward our goal at sufficient speed," Warsh said. That criteria has not been met, he observed.
Inflation risks are to the upside, while labor risks are roughly balanced.
Warsh called the move a "serious decision and a sober decision." He's not going to prejudge any future decisions.

title: The Fed 'removes a dose of accommodation,' Warsh says at press conference
